- If sentiment is consistently low (0.00) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast slope or adding downward bias.
- If sentiment spikes (e.g., 0.20) in recent history, model often underestimates or fails to capture upward momentum; adjust forecast upward, especially early in horizon.
- Model frequently overcorrects after sharp price spikes — reduce forecast slope after 3–5 consecutive high values.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 3–7 days; apply a 1–2 day lead correction if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend after a dip, model often fails to recognize it — increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows sharp rise, model underestimates momentum — increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day if sentiment is positive.
